cvEn:
Yaakov Vinditzki, son of Haim-Zadok and Etka, was born on the 16th of Kislev 5690 (18 December 1929) in the town of Melbe in Poland. When World War II began and the Nazi forces occupied the town, the entire family set out on wanderings that took them as far as the depths of Siberia. The family suffered hunger and disease, which caused the death of the father and of his younger sister.

In 1946, when departure from Russia began, Yaakov returned with his brother and mother to Poland, where he joined a training kibbutz and prepared to make aliyah to the Land of Israel. From Poland he moved to training kibbutzim in France and Belgium, and his longing to emigrate grew stronger in his heart.

In 1948 he was drafted into the IDF within the framework of Gahal. After brief training he was sent to the northern front and took part in the conquest of Upper Galilee. In 1947 his brother had come to the country within the framework of Youth Aliyah and had also taken part in the conquest of Upper Galilee. His mother made aliyah during his military service. Upon his discharge he returned to his family and began studying at the Israeli Institute for Correspondence Education, affiliated with the Center for Culture. He was interested in literature and music, and played the trumpet and the mandolin. He began working as a driver and afterwards as a mechanic at the "Ashed" garage.

He fell in the course of performing his duties on the 7th of Sivan 5714 (8 June 1954), while serving as an active reservist, and was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Kiryat Shaul.
